title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Predict Atomic Oxygen Erosion of Polymers in Low Earth Orbit
summary: On the restricted-group test, GPT-4o predicted erosion yield for polymer chemistries excluded from training; adding film thickness or layer count did not materially improve performance, indicating chemistry/exposure variables dominated those bulk descriptors in this dataset. 201 historical NASA-mission measurements, 55 chemistries; random and chemistry-disjoint restricted-group evaluation, with five restricted-group splits testing 29 held-out chemistries (26 for the thickness/layer ablation). Reported OME 0.154 and log-R² 0.719. This is retrospective prediction against measurements, not prospective or new flight validation.
ai_technology: Fine-tuned GPT-4o predicts polymer atomic-oxygen erosion yield from polymer chemistry and exposure descriptors; the model supplies the feature-ablation evidence for the reported descriptor finding.
organization: Department of Chemical Engineering, University of California, Santa Barbara, Santa Barbara, California, USA
